Fit a brms style mixed-effects model

Source: R/hib_fit_brms.R
hib_fit_brms.Rd

This function fits a brms model using the supplied database, formula and other function arguments tuning the model fitting process

Usage

hib_fit_brms(
  obj,
  form,
  family = stats::gaussian,
  weight_specs = list(weights = NULL, weight_type = NULL),
  scale_specs = list(covars_to_scale = NULL, scale_func = NULL),
  relevel_specs = c(NULL),
  ...
)

Arguments

obj

A HibDatabase object or a list of them.

form

A formula in the style of brms (as in lme4) - including fixed and random effects.

family

A family function, e.g. gaussian, poisson - as allowed by brms

weight_specs

A list containing "weights" and "weight_type". weights is a numeric vector containing the relative weights to assign to each dataset/site, should sum to 1. weight_type is a character, specifying either "dataset" or "site" - i.e. should the weights argument assign relative weights to whole datasets, or for sites in each dataset. Note: if using this argument, the supplied formula should have a response of the form y | weights(data_weight) ~. The data_weight variable will be generated within the function call.

scale_specs

A list containing "covars_to_scale" and "scale_func". covars_to_scale is a character vector of numeric covariates that should be scaled prior to modelling. scale_func is a function that will be used to scale the specified covariates - if NULL, base::scale() will be used.

relevel_specs

A named vector where each item is: "<covar_to_relevel_name>" = "<base_level>".

...

Any other named arguments that can be passed to brms::brm(), e.g., prior, data2

Details

Expects a HibDatabase object...

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  mod <- hib_fit_brms(obj, y ~ x + ( 1 | a ), ...)
} # }
